svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram of a put: Client, S3 front, Proxy, Hot tier, Cold tier. The front reads the content headers, user metadata, tags and declared checksums, hashes the body once for every digest, hands the proxy the body with a slot that fills at the last chunk, the tier publishes the object and its record, the entry moves to PENDING, the answer carries the ETag; later the leader copies the object with its record to cold.
svg.title: A put with metadata and checksums: one pass, the record lands with the object
svg.text: A put with metadata and checksums: one pass, the record lands with the object
Client
S3 front
Proxy
Hot tier
Cold tier
0 PUT key: Content-Type, x-amz-meta-*, x-amz-tagging, x-amz-checksum-*
1 Attrs = content headers, user metadata, tags, declared checksums.
Too large or malformed: 400 before any byte is read (MetadataTooLarge, InvalidTag)
2 Accumulator over each chunk as it passes: md5, crc64nvme, the declared one (and sha256 when signed)
3 put_stream_with(key, len, body, Landing { attrs, digest slot })
4 take entry, HEAD both tiers (unchanged, section 5 Put)
5 chunks, streamed (the tier hashes its own tag as before)
6 Last chunk: declared checksums, Content-MD5 and signed sha256 compared.
Mismatch: 400 BadDigest, nothing published. Match: the digest slot is filled
7 publish object create-only, then its record (sidecar on dir:)
8 CAS entry (PUT, HELD) to (PUT, PENDING): the acknowledgement
9 200, ETag: "md5 hex", x-amz-checksum-* of the object
Later: the leader copies the object, and the record goes with it
10 open_read key: size, tag, record (one call, as for a get)
11 put_stream_with(key, body, Landing { record }): headers and record up front on S3
The record is published after the object it describes and is trusted only when its tag and size equal the object's; a put that cannot publish
its record removes the object, as for a failed sync.
The digests are computed once, in the front, while the bytes pass. No tier re-reads the object for them.
